## Physical AI and Embodied Systems Notation {#sec-notation-physical}

Physical AI and embodied machine learning systems merge three distinct technical traditions:

1. **Machine Learning and Deep Learning** (statistical optimization, transformers, diffusion policies, imitation learning, autoregression, Action Chunking with Transformers).
2. **Robotics, Mechanics, and Classical Control** (multibody dynamics, $SE(3)$ Lie groups, rigid-body kinematics, Lyapunov stability, Control Barrier Functions, contact mechanics, actuator drive physics).
3. **Embedded Systems and Real-Time Architectures** (system-on-chip interconnects, cache and memory bus contention, hardware interrupt latency, seqlocks, CAN-FD/EtherCAT, intent leases, fail-safe interlocks).

Because each discipline developed its mathematical notation independently over decades, combining them creates severe symbol collisions, the "traditional warts" of cyber-physical engineering. For example, writing $\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(\mathbf{a} \mid \mathbf{q})$ when $\theta$ also denotes joint angles, or writing $\mathbf{a}_t$ for an action when $\mathbf{a}$ denotes Cartesian acceleration or barrier constraints, confuses spatial mechanics with parameter optimization and control execution authority.

Below, we formalize the cross-discipline disambiguation contract, state the governing relationships of embodied systems, and tabulate the canonical symbols used throughout this book. Every symbol of the series core keeps its core meaning here: $T$ is time, $\text{BW}$ bandwidth, $L_{\text{lat}}$ latency, $R_{\text{peak}}$ peak rate, $O$ operations, $I$ arithmetic intensity, $D_{\text{vol}}$ bytes moved, $\mathcal{L}$ loss, $\eta$ learning rate, and $\mathcal{O}(\cdot)$ asymptotic cost. Serving and memory arithmetic on the robot's computer uses those symbols, with a subscript naming the instance ($\text{BW}_{\text{mem}}$, $O_{\text{prefill}}$).

## Cross-Discipline Disambiguation and Traditional Warts {#sec-notation-disambiguation .unlisted}

When physical plant dynamics meet deep neural networks and real-time embedded hardware, common mathematical shorthand breaks down. The conventions below resolve these cross-domain collisions systematically:

A subscripted Greek $\tau$ marks a time only for these named constants and delays: $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ (pre-brake delay, excluding $\Delta_{\text{da}}$) and its ceiling $\tau_{\text{delay},\max}$, $\tau_e = L_{\text{phase}}/R_{\text{phase}}$ (electrical), $\tau_{\text{th}} = R_{\text{th}} C_{\text{th}}$ (thermal, with stage constants such as $\tau_{\text{th,cu}}$ and $\tau_{\text{th,case}}$), $\tau_{\text{fall}}$ (balance divergence), $\tau_{\text{ZOH}}$ (sample-and-hold delay), $\tau_{\text{ev}}$ (evidence horizon), and $\tau_{\text{blend}}$ (authority blend window). Every other interval uses Latin $T$ or $t$: observation age is $t_{\text{age}}$, never $\tau$; leases are $T_{\text{lease}}$, $T_{\text{lease,man}}$, and $T_{\text{admin}}$; compute and fieldbus times are $T_{\text{comp}}$ and $T_{\text{bus}}$; a pure transport delay is $T_d$. ## Governing Relationships {#sec-notation-governing-laws .unlisted}

Embodied intelligence operates subject to thermodynamic, mechanical, kinematic, and communications constraints. The relationships below state those constraints in the symbols the chapters use.

### 1. Sense-to-actuation delay budget {#sec-notation-embodied-iron-law .unlisted}

Delay converts directly into travel before any retarding force begins. The pre-brake delay $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ runs from the capture of the frame that first shows a hazard to retarding force, excluding the dispatch-to-admission interval $\Delta_{\text{da}}$, which the stopping budget charges against its timing allowance. The stop it leaves, whose travel is $d_{\text{suffix}}(v)$, must fit inside the clear distance, and the spare that remains must pay for $v\,\Delta_{\text{da}}$:

$$\tau_{\text{delay}} = t_{\text{age}} + T_{\text{lease}} + T_{\text{tick}} + T_{\text{bus}} + T_{\text{act}}$$

$$v\,\tau_{\text{delay}} + d_{\text{suffix}}(v) + \delta_{\text{loc}} + \delta_{\text{margin}} + \epsilon_{\text{track}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$$

Inference time is spent on the proposal side of the proposal boundary. It ages the evidence behind a proposal, which the permission path checks against the proposal's expiry, but it is neither a term of $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ nor part of the permission loop's period $T_{\text{tick}}$, because the fallback does not wait for the proposer.

The appendices regroup the same interval for two specific stop paths, and each form defines its own terms. For a stop triggered by lease expiry, $\tau_{\text{delay}} = T_{\text{lease}} + t_{\text{detect}} + T_{\text{hold}} + t_{\text{age}} + T_{\text{act}}$; for a stop triggered by a hazard detector, $\tau_{\text{delay}} = t_{\text{age}} + t_{\text{detect}} + T_{\text{compute}} + T_{\text{bus}} + T_{\text{act}}$.

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                       | **Definition**                     | **Unit**              | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|:---------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:----------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\tau_{\text{delay}}$**        | **Pre-Brake Delay**                | $\text{ms}$           | Time from capture of the frame that first shows a hazard to the onset of retarding force, excluding $\Delta_{\text{da}}$; the machine travels $v\,(\tau_{\text{delay}} + \Delta_{\text{da}})$ before braking begins. Its allowed ceiling is $\tau_{\text{delay},\max}$.                                                    |
| **$t_{\text{age}}$**             | **Observation Age**                | $\text{ms}$           | Age of the state the permission path acts on, from the exposure midpoint at the sensor to the decision, which enters $\tau_{\text{delay}}$. Its perception-side terms are the exposure midpoint $\tfrac{1}{2}t_{\text{exp}}$, sensor readout, transfer, and perception processing; a bound on it is $t_{\text{age},\max}$. |
| **$T_{\text{lease}}$**           | **Chunk Lease**                    | $\text{ms}$           | Longest interval an admitted chunk may keep driving the actuators without renewal, which enters $\tau_{\text{delay}}$; chosen, then checked against the ceiling the stopping budget derives.                                                                                                                               |
| **$T_{\text{chunk}}$**           | **Chunk Renewal Period**           | $\text{ms}$           | Interval between successful admissions of the chunk policy; with $T_{\text{jitter}}$ it sets the floor of the lease rule, $T_{\text{chunk}} + T_{\text{jitter}} < T_{\text{lease}}$ (@eq-nervous-lease-rule).                                                                                                              |
| **$T_{\text{jitter}}$**          | **Renewal-Jitter Allowance**       | $\text{ms}$           | Allowance for variation in the interval between successful admissions; chosen, then checked against measured renewal intervals.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **$T_{\text{tick}}$**            | **Permission-Loop Period**         | $\text{ms}$           | Period of the permission loop, which enters $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ because a hazard may wait up to one period before it is checked.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **$T_{\text{bus}}$**             | **Command Transport Time**         | $\text{ms}$           | Fieldbus delivery time from the permission path to the drive, which enters $\tau_{\text{delay}}$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **$T_{\text{act}}$**             | **Actuator Response Time**         | $\text{ms}$           | Time from a delivered stop command to retarding force, including gate-drive and current rise, which enters $\tau_{\text{delay}}$.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **$t_{\text{detect}}$**          | **Detection Interval**             | $\text{ms}$           | Recognition or expiry-detection time after the decision-start epoch, not already charged to $t_{\text{age}}$; a term of the lease-expiry and hazard-detection forms of $\tau_{\text{delay}}$.                                                                                                                              |
| **$T_{\text{hold}}$**            | **Fallback Hold**                  | $\text{ms}$           | Optional, separately authorized hold or fault-confirmation interval before the stop command reaches the drive; zero when the stop path has none.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **$t_{\text{sense}}$**           | **Sensor Integration Time**        | $\text{ms}$           | Half the exposure duration (its integration midpoint), ADC conversion, and sensor readout latency; contributes to $t_{\text{age}}$.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **$t_{\text{xfer}}$**            | **Interconnect Transfer Time**     | $\text{ms}$           | DMA bus streaming, PCIe handoff, and serializer-deserializer (SerDes) link latency; contributes to $t_{\text{age}}$.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **$t_{\text{infer}}$**           | **Proposer Inference Time**        | $\text{ms}$           | Time for one complete evaluation of the learned proposer (prefill and decode); spent above the proposal boundary and outside the permission loop's period.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **$\Delta_{\text{da}}$**         | **Dispatch-to-Admission Interval** | $\text{ms}$           | Elapsed time from perception dispatch to the admission of the candidate it conditions; evidence keeps aging through it. Not a term of $\tau_{\text{delay}}$; its travel $v\,\Delta_{\text{da}}$ is charged against the stopping budget's timing allowance.                                                                 |
| **$T_{\Sigma,1}, T_{\Sigma,2}$** | **Takeover Response Time**         | $\text{ms}, \text{s}$ | Human response plus console transport for an in-loop ($T_{\Sigma,1}$) and an out-of-loop ($T_{\Sigma,2}$) takeover; it adds to $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ while the machine waits for the person.                                                                                                                               |
| **$T_{\text{deadline}}$**        | **Deadline**                       | $\text{ms}, \text{s}$ | A duration budget a computation or handover must meet (the series symbol); qualifiers name the instance, as in $T_{\text{deadline,fallback}}$, the latest permissible wait before the fallback must begin. A deadline stated as a clock instant is lowercase, $t_{\text{deadline}}$ or $t_{\text{deadline,stop}}$.         |
| **$T_{\text{timeout}}$**         | **Handover Timeout**               | $\text{s}$            | Timer an arbiter sets for an unacknowledged handover, $T_{\text{timeout}} = \max(0, \min(T_{\text{config}}, T_{\text{deadline,fallback}}))$, where $T_{\text{config}}$ is the protocol ceiling.                                                                                                                            |
| **$t_{\text{commit}}$**          | **Commitment Instant**             | $\text{s}$            | Instant after which a receding-horizon plan's prefix is committed and can no longer be replaced by a new proposal.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **$t_{\text{onset}}$**           | **Hazard Onset**                   | $\text{s}$            | Instant at which a hazard first becomes physically present, the reference from which detection and stopping intervals are measured.                                                                                                                                                                                        |

:::

### Leases {#sec-notation-leases .unlisted}

A lease is authority that lapses unless it is renewed. The book uses six kinds:

::: {tbl-colwidths="[16,16,68]"}

| **Lease**                | **Symbol**                       | **Distinction**                                                                                                                                                                      |
|:-------------------------|:---------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Execution lease**      | remaining $T_{\text{lease,rem}}$ | Any authority an admitted command source holds to keep driving the actuators without renewal; it begins at admission, and its expiry invokes the state-matched fallback.             |
| **Chunk lease**          | $T_{\text{lease}}$               | The execution lease of the autonomous chunk policy, renewed by each admitted chunk; it enters $\tau_{\text{delay}}$.                                                                 |
| **Manual lease**         | $T_{\text{lease,man}}$           | The execution lease of a human operator in manual mode, renewed by authenticated heartbeats; it replaces the chunk lease in $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ while the operator drives.         |
| **Administrative lease** | $T_{\text{admin}}$               | The host-silence bound inside an intent lease: how long the application processor may hold a goal without renewing it.                                                               |
| **Intent lease**         | expiry $t_{\text{intent\_exp}}$  | The record that grants a grounded target and effort ceilings, never a path; it expires at the earliest of its evidence horizon, its administrative lease, and its stopping deadline. |
| **Hardware lease**       | (mechanism)                      | The countdown timer on the safety microcontroller that enforces any of these expiries even when the process that issued the authority has hung.                                      |

:::

### 2. Action-chunk streaming cadence {#sec-notation-chunking-cadence .unlisted}

Cognitive neural policies cannot execute at kilohertz frequencies due to memory bandwidth limits. Action chunking predicts an action trajectory of horizon $H$ at a lower cognitive frequency $f_{\text{policy}}$, while the chunk's waypoints are consumed at $f_{\text{exec}}$. The memory streaming latency must remain bounded by the chunk execution window, less the compute term $T_{\text{compute}}$ of the iron law:

$$t_{\text{stream}} = \frac{M_{\text{weights}}}{\text{BW}_{\text{mem}}} \le \frac{H}{f_{\text{exec}}} - T_{\text{compute}}$$

A decoder that streams its nonresident weights once per emitted token spends, for $S_{\text{out}}$ emitted tokens, the inference time

$$t_{\text{infer}} \approx \max\!\left(\frac{O_{\text{prefill}}}{\eta_{\text{hw}}\,R_{\text{peak}}},\ \frac{M_{\text{weights}}}{\text{BW}_{\text{mem}}}\right) + (S_{\text{out}} - 1)\,\frac{M_{\text{weights}}}{\text{BW}_{\text{mem}}}$$

which caps the fresh-evaluation rate at $f \le \text{BW}_{\text{mem}}/M_{\text{weights}}$ when every evaluation streams the weights. The symbols are the series core's: $O_{\text{prefill}}$ counts the prefill's operations, $R_{\text{peak}}$ is the processor's peak rate at the activation precision, $\eta_{\text{hw}}$ is the fraction of it the prefill achieves, and $I$ is the arithmetic intensity that decides which term binds.

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                   | **Definition**                 | **Unit**    | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                |
|:-----------------------------|:-------------------------------|:------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$H$**                      | **Action Chunk Horizon**       | Time steps  | Number of contiguous future action steps generated in a single policy forward pass ($H=16$ on the mobile manipulator; 16 to 64 steps in the literature). |
| **$d_a$**                    | **Action Dimension**           | Integer     | Number of components of one action $\mathbf{a}_t$; a chunk $\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}$ has $H \times d_a$ entries.                                              |
| **$\text{BW}_{\text{mem}}$** | **Sustained Memory Bandwidth** | bytes/s     | Achievable memory throughput of the SoC or accelerator memory subsystem (e.g., LPDDR5, HBM); the core's $\text{BW}$ at the memory interface.             |
| **$t_{\text{stream}}$**      | **Parameter Streaming Time**   | $\text{ms}$ | Time required to stream non-resident model weights into execution registers.                                                                             |
| **$f_{\text{exec}}$**        | **Action Execution Rate**      | $\text{Hz}$ | Temporal consumption rate of chunked waypoints along the planned trajectory ($100\text{ Hz}$ to $1\text{ kHz}$).                                         |
| **$S_{\text{out}}$**         | **Emitted Token Count**        | tokens      | Output tokens an autoregressive decoder emits per evaluation; the core's sequence length $S$ for the decoded part. Never $D$, which is dataset size.     |

:::

### 3. The dynamic stopping, braking, and safe-set invariants {#sec-notation-stopping-invariant .unlisted}

Forward invariance of the safe set $\mathcal{C}$ requires that the machine can arrest all motion before it reaches the boundary. The stopping distance combines the travel during the pre-brake delay with the braking distance, and its margins are added in the inequality of the delay budget above:

$$d_{\text{stop}}(v) = v\,\tau_{\text{delay}} + d_{\text{suffix}}(v), \qquad d_{\text{suffix}}(v) = \frac{v^2}{2a_{\text{brake}}} + \frac{v\,a_{\text{brake}}}{2j_{\max}} \quad (v \ge a_{\text{brake}}^2/j_{\max})$$

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                                | **Definition**                 | **Unit**                       | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$d_{\text{stop}}$**                     | **Stopping Distance**          | $\text{m}$                     | Distance required to bring the plant to rest from speed $v$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **$D_{\text{clear}}$**                    | **Clear Distance**             | $\text{m}$                     | Clear distance from the machine to the boundary it must not cross; the subscript keeps it distinct from dataset size $D$.                                                                                                                                                     |
| **$v$**                                   | **Speed at Detection**         | $\text{m/s}$                   | Speed of the machine at the moment the hazard is detected.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **$v_{\max}$**                            | **Speed Bound**                | $\text{m/s}$                   | Largest speed the machine, a tracked object, or an approaching body is credited with in a budget; the bounding speed in $\Delta t_{\text{fresh}} \le e_{\max}/v_{\max}$.                                                                                                      |
| **$a_{\text{brake}}$**                    | **Credible Deceleration**      | $\text{m/s}^2$                 | Validated low tail of the deceleration the machine achieves under its stated conditions, not the datasheet peak.                                                                                                                                                              |
| **$a_{\max}$**                            | **Profile Acceleration Bound** | $\text{m/s}^2$                 | Largest acceleration or deceleration a planned or interpolated profile may command; for the base's resident stop it is set to $a_{\text{brake}}$.                                                                                                                             |
| **$a_{\text{net}}, \alpha_{\text{net}}$** | **Net Braking Deceleration**   | $\text{m/s}^2, \text{rad/s}^2$ | Linear or angular deceleration left after a gravity or load bias torque $\tau_{\text{bias}}$ is subtracted from the actuator's braking capacity, in the direction of travel.                                                                                                  |
| **$d_{\text{suffix}}(v)$**                | **Resident Stop Distance**     | $\text{m}$                     | Travel of the resident stop from speed $v$: $v^2/(2a_{\text{brake}})$ for constant-deceleration braking; for the jerk-limited stop of @eq-plan-c2-stopping-suffix, that term plus the jerk ramps' $v\,a_{\text{brake}}/(2j_{\max})$ once $v \ge a_{\text{brake}}^2/j_{\max}$. |
| **$\delta_{\text{loc}}$**                 | **Localization Bound**         | $\text{m}$                     | Bound on localization and state-estimation error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **$\delta_{\text{margin}}$**              | **Protective Clearance**       | $\text{m}$                     | Fixed, nonzero protective clearance between the machine envelope and the boundary.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **$\epsilon_{\text{track}}$**             | **Tracking-Error Bound**       | $\text{m}$                     | Bound on the deviation between the commanded and the executed trajectory, stated by the enforcement record.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **$v_h$**                                 | **Human Walking-Speed Bound**  | $\text{m/s}$                   | Walking-speed bound for a person approaching the machine, used in the form its safety standard states.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **$j_{\max}$**                            | **Jerk Limit**                 | $\text{m/s}^3$                 | Maximum rate of change of deceleration; sets the jerk ramps of the resident stop in $d_{\text{suffix}}(v)$ (@eq-plan-c2-stopping-suffix) and bounds the bumpless-transfer window $\tau_{\text{blend}}$.                                                                       |

:::

### 4. The digital sampling zero-order hold (ZOH) phase margin {#sec-notation-zoh-law .unlisted}

Holding discrete control commands constant over sampling period $T_s = 1/f_s$ introduces an effective transport delay of half the sample period, which with the enforcer's compute time and the fieldbus transit erodes feedback stability margins:

$$\tau_{\text{ZOH}} = \frac{T_s}{2}, \qquad \Delta\phi = \omega_c \left( \frac{T_s}{2} + T_{\text{comp}} + T_{\text{bus}} \right), \qquad \text{PM}_{\text{net}} = \text{PM}_{\text{plant}} - \Delta\phi > 0$$

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                   | **Definition**                    | **Unit**                    | **Notes**                                                                                                                                         |
|:-----------------------------|:----------------------------------|:----------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\tau_{\text{ZOH}}$**      | **ZOH Transport Delay**           | $\text{s}$                  | Equivalent continuous delay introduced by discrete Zero-Order Hold reconstruction ($T_s / 2$).                                                    |
| **$T_s, f_s$**               | **Sampling Period and Rate**      | $\text{s}, \text{Hz}$       | Discrete controller execution period and frequency ($f_s = 1/T_s$).                                                                               |
| **$T_{\text{comp}}$**        | **Enforcer Compute Time**         | $\text{s}$                  | Time the enforcer takes to evaluate its constraints within one control period; with $T_{\text{bus}}$ it adds to the ZOH delay.                    |
| **$T_d$**                    | **Pure Transport Delay**          | $\text{s}$                  | A fixed delay in a feedback or communication channel, contributing phase lag $\omega T_d$ at frequency $\omega$.                                  |
| **$\omega_c$**               | **Open-Loop Crossover Frequency** | $\text{rad/s}$              | Frequency at which open-loop gain $\lvert L(j\omega_c) \rvert = 1$ ($0\text{ dB}$).                                                               |
| **$\Delta \phi$**            | **Phase Lag Degradation**         | $\text{rad}$ / $\text{deg}$ | Phase erosion at crossover ($\Delta \phi \approx 28.65^\circ \cdot (\omega_c / f_s)$ from the hold alone) depleting closed-loop stability margin. |
| **$\text{PM}_{\text{net}}$** | **Net Phase Margin**              | $\text{deg}$                | Residual stability margin ($\text{PM}_{\text{plant}} - \Delta \phi > 0$) preventing contact chatter.                                              |

:::

### 5. Actuator electromechanical and thermal rise invariants {#sec-notation-actuator-laws .unlisted}

Actuators are constrained by copper winding heating, DC bus rail droop, and magnetic saturation. Sustainable torque output is governed by the coupled electromechanical balance, written per joint with scalar torque:

$$V_{\text{bus}} = L_{\text{phase}} \frac{di_q}{dt} + R(T_{\text{wind}})\, i_q + K_e \omega_m, \qquad C_{\text{th}} \frac{dT_{\text{wind}}}{dt} = i_q^2 R(T_{\text{wind}}) - \frac{T_{\text{wind}} - T_{\text{amb}}}{R_{\text{th}}}, \qquad \tau = \eta_{\text{gear}} N_{\text{gear}} K_t i_q$$

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                               | **Definition**                       | **Unit**                                             | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|:-----------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$K_t, K_e$**                           | **Torque and Back-EMF Constants**    | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m/A}, \text{V}\cdot\text{s/rad}$ | Motor electromechanical coupling constants linking winding current to rotor shaft torque and rotor speed to back-EMF voltage ($K_t \approx K_e$ in SI units).                                                                    |
| **$i_q$**                                | **Torque-Producing Current**         | $\text{A}$                                           | Quadrature-axis current of a field-oriented drive, $\tau_{\text{motor}} = K_t i_q$. Bare $I$ is never a current, because the series core reserves it for arithmetic intensity.                                                   |
| **$I_{\text{phase}}$**                   | **Motor Phase RMS Current**          | $\text{A}$                                           | RMS phase current driving the stator windings of a brushless PM motor; an uppercase $I$ with a subscript names an RMS value or rating.                                                                                           |
| **$I_{\text{cont}}, I_{\text{peak}}$**   | **Continuous / Peak Current**        | $\text{A}$                                           | RMS current ratings bounded by winding insulation class and inverter MOSFET dissipation.                                                                                                                                         |
| **$L_{\text{phase}}, R_{\text{phase}}$** | **Phase Inductance and Resistance**  | $\text{H}, \Omega$                                   | Stator winding inductance and DC resistance; they set $\tau_e = L_{\text{phase}}/R_{\text{phase}}$.                                                                                                                              |
| **$R(T_{\text{wind}})$**                 | **Temperature-Dependent Resistance** | $\Omega$                                             | Stator copper resistance at winding temperature $T_{\text{wind}}$: $R(T_{\text{wind}}) = R_0 [1 + \alpha_{\text{Cu}}(T_{\text{wind}} - T_0)]$ with $\alpha_{\text{Cu}} = 0.00393\text{ K}^{-1}$.                                 |
| **$R_{\text{th}}$**                      | **Thermal Resistance**               | $\text{K/W}$                                         | Lumped thermal resistance from stator windings to the ambient environment; path segments carry a second subscript ($R_{\text{th,JA}}$, $R_{\text{th,JC}}$, $R_{\text{th,wc}}$, $R_{\text{th,ca}}$) and add in series.            |
| **$C_{\text{th}}$**                      | **Stator Thermal Capacitance**       | $\text{J/K}$                                         | Lumped heat capacity of the motor core, windings, and potting compound.                                                                                                                                                          |
| **$\tau_e$**                             | **Electrical Time Constant**         | $\text{s}$                                           | Winding current rise time constant $\tau_e = L_{\text{phase}}/R_{\text{phase}}$; current reaches $1 - e^{-1}$ of its target in $\tau_e$.                                                                                         |
| **$\tau_{\text{th}}$**                   | **Thermal Time Constant**            | $\text{s}$                                           | Actuator heating characteristic time constant ($\tau_{\text{th}} = R_{\text{th}} C_{\text{th}}$, typically $60\text{--}300\text{ s}$); a single stage takes a second subscript ($\tau_{\text{th,cu}}$, $\tau_{\text{th,case}}$). |
| **$T_{\text{wind}}, T_{\text{amb}}$**    | **Winding and Ambient Temperature**  | $\text{K}$ or $^\circ\text{C}$                       | The thermal model's state and boundary temperatures; the other temperatures follow the subscript rule of the disambiguation table ($T_{\text{j}}$, $T_{\text{case}}$, $T_{\text{limit}}$, $T_\infty$, $T_0$).                    |
| **$\Delta T$**                           | **Joulean Temperature Rise**         | $\text{K}$                                           | Steady-state or transient thermal rise above ambient ($\Delta T = P_{\text{loss}} R_{\text{th}}$); never a time interval.                                                                                                        |
| **$D_{\text{cycle}}$**                   | **Actuator Duty Cycle**              | $[0, 1]$                                             | Ratio of active pulse duration to cycle period ($t_{\text{on}} / (t_{\text{on}} + t_{\text{off}})$) preventing thermal runaway.                                                                                                  |
| **$\Delta V_{\text{droop}}$**            | **DC Bus Dynamic Rail Droop**        | $\text{V}$                                           | Transient voltage collapse ($\Delta I R_{\text{bus}} + L_{\text{bus}}\frac{dI}{dt} + \frac{\Delta I \Delta t}{2 C_{\text{bus}}}$) under step motor current loads, which can trigger an undervoltage reset.                       |

:::

### 6. Shielded hazard architecture and statistical exposure bound {#sec-notation-shield-laws .unlisted}

Catastrophic failure rates in embodied systems cannot be certified through stochastic testing alone. For a defined hazard class $h$, a deterministic safety shield bounds the system's hazard rate, while zero-failure exposure follows the Rule of Three:

$$\lambda_{\text{system},h} \le \lambda_{\text{proposal},h} (1 - c_h) + \lambda_{\text{other}} \le \lambda_{\text{target}}, \qquad T \ge \frac{-\ln \alpha_{\text{sig}}}{\lambda_{\text{target}}}$$

Here $T$ is the zero-incident operating exposure, in hours. Per-trial campaigns use the same bound in probability form, $n \ge \ln\alpha_{\text{sig}}/\ln p_{\text{target}} \approx 3/(1 - p_{\text{target}})$.

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                                     | **Definition**                      | **Unit**        | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|:-----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------|:----------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\lambda_{\text{system},h}$**                | **System Hazard Rate**              | $\text{h}^{-1}$ | Certified dangerous failure rate of the integrated cyber-physical machine for hazard class $h$.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **$\lambda_{\text{proposal},h}$**              | **Hazardous Proposal Rate**         | $\text{h}^{-1}$ | Arrival rate of unshielded hazardous action proposals the policy emits before the permission layer, measured against a counterfactual oracle.                                                                                                                                   |
| **$c_h$**                                      | **Shield Interception Coverage**    | Dimensionless   | Verified conditional probability that the shield intercepts a hazardous proposal of class $h$, evaluated over the states in which the policy errs.                                                                                                                              |
| **$\lambda_{\text{other}}$**                   | **Hardware and Common-Cause Rate**  | $\text{h}^{-1}$ | Independently bounded hardware-fault and common-cause hazard rate the shield cannot intercept; the floor $\lambda_{\text{system},h}$ reaches when $c_h = 1$.                                                                                                                    |
| **$\lambda_{\text{target}}$**                  | **Target Hazard Rate**              | $\text{h}^{-1}$ | Tolerable dangerous failure rate assigned to the safety function by risk assessment, in the band its governing standard defines.                                                                                                                                                |
| **$C_{\text{diag}}$**                          | **Diagnostic Coverage**             | Dimensionless   | Rate-weighted fraction of hardware faults whose hazardous effect is mitigated, $\lambda_{\text{unmitigated}} = \lambda_{\text{raw}}(1 - C_{\text{diag}})$; the hardware counterpart of $c_h$, which covers policy proposals.                                                    |
| **$p_{\text{fail}}, p_{\text{target}}$**       | **Per-Trial Probabilities**         | Dimensionless   | Per-trial failure probability, and the per-trial success probability a campaign must demonstrate; trial counts follow $n \ge \ln\alpha_{\text{sig}}/\ln p_{\text{target}}$.                                                                                                     |
| **$\alpha_{\text{sig}}$**                      | **Statistical Significance Level**  | Dimensionless   | Type I error threshold ($\alpha_{\text{sig}} = 1 - \text{CL}$, e.g., $\alpha_{\text{sig}}=0.05$ for 95% confidence where $-\ln(0.05) \approx 3.0$).                                                                                                                             |
| **$\beta$**                                    | **Type II Error Allowance**         | Dimensionless   | Probability of rejecting an acceptable candidate ($1-\beta$ is the power); with $\alpha_{\text{sig}}$ it sets the SPRT boundaries $\Lambda_{\text{up}}$ and $\Lambda_{\text{lo}}$. Diffusion schedules use indexed $\beta_s$; a KL weight $\beta$ stays local to its objective. |
| **$n$**                                        | **Zero-Failure Trial Count**        | Trials          | Required number of incident-free trials to substantiate $p_{\text{target}}$; for exposure measured in hours, the bound is on $T$ instead.                                                                                                                                       |
| **$\Lambda_m$**                                | **Sequential Log-Likelihood Ratio** | Dimensionless   | After $k$ failures in $m$ trials, $\Lambda_m = k\ln(p_1/p_0) + (m-k)\ln\frac{1-p_1}{1-p_0}$ for per-trial failure probabilities $p_0$ (unacceptable) and $p_1$ (acceptable); SPRT stops when it leaves $(\Lambda_{\text{lo}}, \Lambda_{\text{up}})$.                            |
| **$\Lambda_{\text{up}}, \Lambda_{\text{lo}}$** | **SPRT Boundaries**                 | Dimensionless   | Upper and lower stopping thresholds on $\Lambda_m$, $\Lambda_{\text{up}} \approx \ln((1-\beta)/\alpha_{\text{sig}})$ and $\Lambda_{\text{lo}} \approx \ln(\beta/(1-\alpha_{\text{sig}}))$; never bare $A$ and $B$.                                                              |

:::

## 1. Physical Plant State, Actuation, and Kinematic Topology

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                                     | **Definition**                     | **Unit**                                 | **Notes**                                                                                                                                      |
|:-----------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$s_t \in \mathcal{S}$**                      | **Physical World State**           | Mixed                                    | Ground-truth continuous state of the machine, environment, and physical contacts at time $t$; italic, because it mixes types.                  |
| **$\mathbf{x}$**                               | **Mechanical Plant State**         | $\text{rad, rad/s}$                      | Generalized state vector $\mathbf{x} = [\mathbf{q}^\top, \dot{\mathbf{q}}^\top]^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ containing positions and velocities. |
| **$\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**              | **Generalized Coordinates**        | $\text{rad}$ or $\text{m}$               | Degrees of freedom describing mechanical articulation (joint angles and prismatic link extensions); entries $q_i$.                             |
| **$\dot{\mathbf{q}} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**        | **Generalized Velocities**         | $\text{rad/s}$ or $\text{m/s}$           | First time derivative of generalized coordinates.                                                                                              |
| **$\ddot{\mathbf{q}} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**       | **Generalized Accelerations**      | $\text{rad/s}^2$ or $\text{m/s}^2$       | Second time derivative of generalized coordinates.                                                                                             |
| **$\boldsymbol{\tau} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**       | **Actuator Torque Vector**         | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ or $\text{N}$    | Generalized forces and torques delivered by actuators at mechanical joints.                                                                    |
| **$\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{q})$**                   | **Generalized Inertia Matrix**     | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$               | Symmetric positive-definite mass/inertia matrix of the articulated multibody plant.                                                            |
| **$\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}})$** | **Coriolis / Centrifugal Matrix**  | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\cdot\text{s/rad}$ | Matrix satisfying $\dot{\mathbf{M}} - 2\mathbf{C}$ skew-symmetry (passivity property).                                                         |
| **$\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q})$**                   | **Gravitational Torque Vector**    | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$                  | Generalized gravitational load acting on links as a function of configuration; a single joint's share is $\tau_g$.                             |
| **$\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{q})$**                   | **Manipulator Jacobian**           | Mixed                                    | Linear mapping $\mathbf{v}_e = \mathbf{J}(\mathbf{q})\dot{\mathbf{q}}$ from joint rates to operational task-space velocity.                    |
| **$w(\mathbf{q})$**                            | **Yoshikawa Manipulability**       | Dimensionless                            | Singularity proximity metric $w(\mathbf{q}) = \sqrt{\det(\mathbf{J}\mathbf{J}^\top)}$ vanishing at kinematic singular configurations.          |
| **$e_{\text{bemf}}$**                          | **Back-EMF Voltage**               | $\text{V}$                               | Opposing voltage $e_{\text{bemf}} = K_e \omega_m$ developed across stator coils by rotor rotation.                                             |
| **$J_{\text{rotor}}, J_{\text{load}}$**        | **Rotor and Load Inertia**         | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$               | Moment of inertia of motor rotor shaft and coupled mechanical load.                                                                            |
| **$J_{\text{ref}}$**                           | **Reflected Rotor Inertia**        | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$               | Effective inertia $J_{\text{ref}} = N_{\text{gear}}^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$ amplified quadratically by gearbox ratio.                              |
| **$J_{\text{eff}}$**                           | **Effective Joint Inertia**        | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$               | Total inertia seen at one joint, link and payload plus $J_{\text{ref}}$; the inertia in single-joint torque and acceleration budgets.          |
| **$N_{\text{gear}}$**                          | **Gear Reduction Ratio**           | Dimensionless                            | Transmission reduction ratio ($N_{\text{gear}} = \omega_m/\omega_j \gg 1$) between motor rotor and joint output shaft; never bare $N$.         |
| **$N^*$**                                      | **Optimal Inertia-Matching Ratio** | Dimensionless                            | Ratio $N^* = \sqrt{J_{\text{load}} / J_{\text{rotor}}}$ maximizing load angular acceleration under peak torque.                                |
| **$\eta_{\text{gear}}$**                       | **Transmission Efficiency**        | Dimensionless                            | Mechanical power transmission efficiency ($0 < \eta_{\text{gear}} \le 1$); never bare $\eta$, which is the learning rate.                      |
| **$\tau_{\text{hold}}, \tau_{\text{peak}}$**   | **Continuous / Peak Torque**       | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$                  | Thermally continuous holding torque and transient peak acceleration torque.                                                                    |

:::

## 2. Rigid-Body Contact Mechanics, Friction Cones, and Centroidal Dynamics

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                                       | **Definition**                   | **Unit**                            | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|:-------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------|:------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\mathbf{S} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times (n+6)}$** | **Actuation Selection Matrix**   | Matrix                              | Matrix $[\mathbf{0}_{n \times 6}, \mathbf{I}_{n \times n}]$ projecting generalized forces onto actuated joints in floating-base systems.                                                                        |
| **$\mathbf{f}_k \in \mathbb{R}^3$**              | **Contact Force Vector**         | $\text{N}$                          | Physical contact force exerted by environment on contact patch $k$ ($\mathbf{f}_k = [\mathbf{f}_{k, \parallel}^\top, f_{k, \perp}]^\top$); always indexed by the contact.                                       |
| **$\mathbf{J}_k(\mathbf{q})$**                   | **Contact Point Jacobian**       | Mixed                               | Mapping joint velocities to contact patch Cartesian linear velocity: $\dot{\mathbf{p}}_k = \mathbf{J}_k(\mathbf{q}) \dot{\mathbf{q}}$.                                                                          |
| **$f_{k, \perp}$**                               | **Normal Contact Force**         | $\text{N}$                          | Unilateral compressive force ($f_{k, \perp} = \mathbf{f}_k^\top \hat{\mathbf{n}}_k \ge 0$) perpendicular to contact plane.                                                                                      |
| **$\mathbf{f}_{k, \parallel}$**                  | **Tangential Contact Shear**     | $\text{N}$                          | Friction traction force tangential to contact plane ($\mathbf{f}_{k, \parallel} = \mathbf{f}_k - f_{k, \perp} \hat{\mathbf{n}}_k$).                                                                             |
| **$\mu$**                                        | **Coulomb Friction Coefficient** | Dimensionless                       | Static/kinetic coefficient bounding friction cone: $\lVert \mathbf{f}_{k, \parallel} \rVert \le \mu f_{k, \perp}$.                                                                                              |
| **$\mathbf{c} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**                | **Center of Mass (CoM)**         | $\text{m}$                          | Spatial coordinates of the total articulated body mass centroid ($\mathbf{c} = \frac{1}{m} \sum m_i \mathbf{p}_i$).                                                                                             |
| **$\mathbf{h}_{\text{lin}} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**   | **Centroidal Linear Momentum**   | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$          | Total plant linear momentum ($\mathbf{h}_{\text{lin}} = m \dot{\mathbf{c}}$), governed by $\dot{\mathbf{h}}_{\text{lin}} = \sum \mathbf{f}_k + m \mathbf{g}_0$, with gravitational acceleration $\mathbf{g}_0$. |
| **$\mathbf{h}_{\text{ang}} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**   | **Centroidal Angular Momentum**  | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}$ | Angular momentum about CoM: $\dot{\mathbf{h}}_{\text{ang}} = \sum (\mathbf{p}_k - \mathbf{c}) \times \mathbf{f}_k + \boldsymbol{\tau}_k$.                                                                       |
| **$\mathbf{p}_{\text{ZMP}} \in \mathbb{R}^2$**   | **Zero Moment Point (ZMP)**      | $\text{m}$                          | Ground-plane point where net horizontal tipping moment vanishes; must reside in $\text{Conv}(\{\mathbf{p}_k\})$.                                                                                                |
| **$e \in [0, 1]$**                               | **Coefficient of Restitution**   | Dimensionless                       | Kinematic velocity rebound ratio during non-smooth impact ($\dot{q}^+ = -e \dot{q}^-$).                                                                                                                         |
| **$k_{\text{contact}}, k_H$**                    | **Contact Stiffness**            | $\text{N/m}$                        | Elastic stiffness of a structural contact, and of the human body region $H$ in an impact (with its effective mass $m_H$), in the form ISO/TS 15066 states.                                                      |
| **$m_{\text{eff}}$**                             | **Effective Impact Mass**        | $\text{kg}$                         | Apparent mass of moving kinematic links along collision trajectory ($m_{\text{eff}} = (\mathbf{u}_{\text{dir}}^\top \mathbf{M}^{-1} \mathbf{u}_{\text{dir}})^{-1}$).                                            |
| **$m_{\text{red}}$**                             | **Reduced Impact Mass**          | $\text{kg}$                         | Two-body reduced mass of a collision, $m_{\text{red}} = (1/m_{\text{eff}} + 1/m_H)^{-1}$, which sets the transferred energy.                                                                                    |
| **$F_{\text{unbraked}}$**                        | **Unbraked Impact Force**        | $\text{N}$                          | Transient collision force peak ($F_{\text{unbraked}} = v_{\max} \sqrt{k_H m_{\text{red}}}$) governed by ISO/TS 15066.                                                                                           |
| **$E_{k, \text{allow}}$**                        | **Allowable Collision Energy**   | $\text{Joules (J)}$                 | Statutory kinetic energy limit ($\frac{1}{2} m_{\text{red}} v^2 \le E_{k, \text{allow}}$) for transient collaborative contact.                                                                                  |

:::

## 3. Geometry, Spatial Transformations, and Perception Projections

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                                                       | **Definition**                         | **Unit**                       | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|:-----------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$SE(3)$**                                                      | **Special Euclidean Group**            | Lie Group                      | Group of 3D rigid-body spatial transformations (translations and rotations: $\mathbb{R}^3 \rtimes SO(3)$).                                                                                                                             |
| **$SO(3)$**                                                      | **Special Orthogonal Group**           | Lie Group                      | Group of $3 \times 3$ proper orthogonal rotation matrices ($\mathbf{R}^\top \mathbf{R} = \mathbf{I}, \det(\mathbf{R}) = +1$).                                                                                                          |
| **$\mathcal{F}_W, \mathcal{F}_B, \mathcal{F}_E$**                | **Coordinate Reference Frames**        | Reference                      | Fixed World frame ($\mathcal{F}_W$), mobile robot Base/body frame ($\mathcal{F}_B$), and End-effector frame ($\mathcal{F}_E$).                                                                                                         |
| **$\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**                                | **Cartesian 3D Position**              | $\text{m}$                     | Position vector $[x, y, z]^\top$ expressing point coordinates in a stated frame.                                                                                                                                                       |
| **$\mathbf{t} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**                                | **Rigid-Transform Translation**        | $\text{m}$                     | Translation part of a rigid transform between two frames (the offset of one frame's origin in the other).                                                                                                                              |
| **$\mathbf{R} \in SO(3)$**                                       | **Directional Cosine Matrix**          | Matrix                         | $3 \times 3$ orthonormal matrix parameterizing spatial attitude and orientation.                                                                                                                                                       |
| **$\mathbf{q}_{\text{quat}} \in \mathbb{H}$**                    | **Unit Quaternion**                    | Dimensionless                  | Hypercomplex orientation vector $[w, x, y, z]^\top$ satisfying $\lVert \mathbf{q}_{\text{quat}} \rVert = 1$.                                                                                                                           |
| **$\mathbf{T}_{A B} \in SE(3)$**                                 | **Homogeneous Transform**              | Matrix                         | $4 \times 4$ matrix $\begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{R}_{AB} & \mathbf{t}_{AB} \\ \mathbf{0}^\top & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ mapping coordinates from frame $B$ into frame $A$.                                                                        |
| **$\mathbf{Ad}_T$**                                              | **Adjoint Representation**             | Matrix                         | $6 \times 6$ transformation matrix mapping spatial twists and wrenches between coordinate frames.                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\boldsymbol{\omega}, \boldsymbol{\alpha} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**  | **Angular Velocity & Acceleration**    | $\text{rad/s}, \text{rad/s}^2$ | Spatial angular velocity and angular acceleration vectors of a rigid body.                                                                                                                                                             |
| **$\mathbf{r}_{P/O} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**                          | **Sensor Lever-Arm Vector**            | $\text{m}$                     | Displacement vector from body rotation origin $O$ to displaced sensor location $P$; its length, or a link's lever arm, is the scalar $r_{\text{arm}}$.                                                                                 |
| **$\mathbf{F}_{\text{fund}}, \mathbf{E}$**                       | **Fundamental and Essential Matrices** | Matrix                         | Two-view epipolar constraint $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_2^\top \mathbf{F}_{\text{fund}}\tilde{\mathbf{m}}_1 = 0$ with $\mathbf{E} = [\mathbf{t}]_\times \mathbf{R}$; the subscript keeps it distinct from the transition matrix $\mathbf{F}$. |
| **$\mathbf{K} \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$**                     | **Pinhole Camera Intrinsics**          | Pixels                         | Calibration matrix $\begin{bmatrix} f_x & 0 & c_x \\ 0 & f_y & c_y \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ parameterizing focal lengths and principal center.                                                                                      |
| **$\mathbf{p}_c = [X_c, Y_c, Z_c]^\top$**                        | **Camera-Frame 3D Coordinate**         | $\text{m}$                     | Metric coordinates of a spatial point in the optical camera frame ($Z_c$ is optical depth).                                                                                                                                            |
| **$[u, v]^\top$, $\tilde{\mathbf{m}}$**                          | **Image Plane Pixel Coordinates**      | Pixels                         | Discrete sensor pixel coordinates ($u \sim f_x \frac{X_c}{Z_c} + c_x$, $v \sim f_y \frac{Y_c}{Z_c} + c_y$), italic as scalars; the homogeneous image point is $\tilde{\mathbf{m}} = [u, v, 1]^\top$, never bold $\mathbf{u}$.          |
| **$t_{\text{exp}}$**                                             | **Exposure Duration**                  | $\text{ms}$                    | Integration time of one camera frame; the frame's timestamp belongs at its midpoint, $t_{\text{exp}}/2$ after exposure starts.                                                                                                         |
| **$T_{\text{inv}}$**                                             | **Belief Invalidation Horizon**        | $\text{ms}$                    | Time since the last supporting evidence after which a belief can no longer be shown to lie inside its task tolerance; a belief expires at $t_0 + T_{\text{inv}}$.                                                                      |
| **$d_{\text{free}}$**                                            | **Free-Space Depth**                   | $\text{m}$                     | Distance from a hull's surface to the nearest cell that is occupied, unknown, or expired, read from an ESDF built with all three treated as obstacles; the budget motion may spend there (@sec-memory-volumetric-metric-maps).         |
| **$t_{\text{row}}$**                                             | **Rolling Shutter Row Readout**        | $\mu\text{s}$                  | Exposure time delta between adjacent CMOS sensor scanlines; row $y$ starts at $t(y) = t_{\text{start}} + y\,t_{\text{row}}$.                                                                                                           |
| **$\Delta \mathbf{x}(y)$**                                       | **Rolling Shutter Distortion**         | $\text{m}$                     | Kinematic skew displacement $\Delta \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{v} \cdot y \cdot t_{\text{row}}$ induced by high-velocity platform motion.                                                                                                    |
| **$\text{tsdf}(\mathbf{p}_{\text{vox}})$**                       | **Truncated Signed Distance**          | $[-1, +1]$                     | Normalized volumetric distance $\text{tsdf}(\mathbf{p}_{\text{vox}}) = \text{clamp}(d(\mathbf{p}_{\text{vox}})/\mu_{\text{tsdf}}, -1, 1)$ of the voxel centered at $\mathbf{p}_{\text{vox}}$ to the nearest surface.                   |
| **$\mu_{\text{tsdf}}$**                                          | **TSDF Truncation Band**               | $\text{m}$                     | Metric thickness of the spatial surface interface band stored in voxel memory.                                                                                                                                                         |
| **$D_t(\mathbf{p}_{\text{vox}}), W_t(\mathbf{p}_{\text{vox}})$** | **TSDF Accumulated Volume**            | Mixed                          | Running weighted signed distance and accumulated visibility weight at the voxel centered at $\mathbf{p}_{\text{vox}}$.                                                                                                                 |
| **$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\text{depth}}$**                         | **Perception Depth Covariance**        | $\text{m}^2$                   | Anisotropic 3D uncertainty covariance ellipsoid associated with stereo/lidar/depth lifting.                                                                                                                                            |
| **$e_0, e_{\max}$**                                              | **Initial and Ceiling Error**          | $\text{m}$                     | Position error of an estimate when its evidence is fresh, and the largest error the task tolerates; $E_0$ and $E_{\max}$ stay energies.                                                                                                |
| **$r_{\text{tol}}$**                                             | **Positional Task Tolerance**          | $\text{m}$                     | Radius within which a target estimate must lie for the task to succeed; paired with the orientation tolerance $\theta_{\text{tol}}$.                                                                                                   |

:::

## 4. Classical and Modern Control (State-Space, Observers, CBF-QPs)

::: {tbl-colwidths="[14,22,12,52]"}

| **Symbol**                                                | **Definition**                            | **Unit**                                | **Notes**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|:----------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\mathbf{A}_{\text{sys}}, \mathbf{B}$**                 | **Linear State-Space Matrices**           | Matrix                                  | Continuous LTI plant: $\dot{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{A}_{\text{sys}}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{B}\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{w}$, observed output $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{H}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{v}_{\text{meas}}$ through the measurement map $\mathbf{H}$ below.                                                               |
| **$\mathbf{w}(t), \mathbf{v}_{\text{meas}}(t)$**          | **Process and Measurement Noise**         | Vector                                  | Zero-mean Gaussian noise vectors with covariance matrices $\mathbf{Q} \succeq 0$ and $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\text{meas}} \succ 0$; bold $\mathbf{R}$ is reserved for rotation.                                                                                                                                  |
| **$\mathbf{F}, \mathbf{H}$**                              | **Transition and Measurement Maps**       | Matrix                                  | Discrete state transition $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k \mid k-1} = \mathbf{F}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1 \mid k-1}$ and measurement map $\mathbf{y}_k = \mathbf{H}\mathbf{x}_k + \mathbf{v}_{\text{meas}}$ of a Kalman filter.                                                                                               |
| **$\mathbf{G}_k$**                                        | **Kalman Gain**                           | Matrix                                  | Weight on the innovation $\boldsymbol{\nu}_k = \mathbf{y}_k - \mathbf{H}\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k \mid k-1}$ in the update step; bold $\mathbf{K}$ is reserved for camera intrinsics.                                                                                                                                |
| **$\mathbf{P} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$**              | **Estimation Error Covariance**           | Matrix                                  | Symmetric positive-definite matrix $\mathbb{E}[(\mathbf{x} - \hat{\mathbf{x}})(\mathbf{x} - \hat{\mathbf{x}})^\top]$ ($\mathbf{P}(t)$ continuous, $\mathbf{P}_{k \mid k}$ discrete) evolving via matrix Riccati equation; $\mathbf{P}_{\text{est}}$ where an LQR cost matrix is also in scope.                 |
| **$\mathbf{O}_{\text{obs}}, \mathbf{O}_{\text{NL}}$**     | **Observability Matrices**                | Matrix                                  | Kalman observability matrix $[\mathbf{H}^\top, (\mathbf{H}\mathbf{A}_{\text{sys}})^\top, \dots]^\top$ and nonlinear Lie matrix $[d\mathbf{h}, dL_{\mathbf{f}}\mathbf{h}, \dots]^\top$; calligraphic $\mathcal{O}(\cdot)$ stays asymptotic cost. The dual controllability matrix is $\mathbf{C}_{\text{ctrb}}$. |
| **$\mathcal{C} \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$**                 | **Forward-Invariant Safe Set**            | Set                                     | Sublevel/superlevel set $\mathcal{C} = \{\mathbf{x} \mid h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0\}$ of plant states where safety invariants are strictly maintained.                                                                                                                                                               |
| **$\partial \mathcal{C}$**                                | **Safety Boundary Manifold**              | Boundary                                | Zero level set $\{\mathbf{x} \mid h(\mathbf{x}) = 0\}$ separating nominal operation from irreversible hazard.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **$h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$**                                 | **Control Barrier Function (CBF)**        | Scalar                                  | Continuously differentiable function whose superlevel set defines forward-invariant set $\mathcal{C}$.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **$\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}), \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})$**      | **Control-Affine Drift and Input Fields** | Vector, Matrix                          | The control-affine model $\dot{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}) + \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})\mathbf{u}$ of barrier analysis; these letters hold only inside that model, where the gravity torque $\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q})$ and contact forces $\mathbf{f}_k$ do not appear.                                     |
| **$L_{\mathbf{f}} h(\mathbf{x})$**                        | **Lie Derivative along Drift**            | $\text{s}^{-1}$                         | Directional gradient derivative $\nabla h(\mathbf{x}) \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})$ along unforced plant dynamics.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **$L_{\mathbf{g}} h(\mathbf{x})$**                        | **Lie Derivative along Control**          | Vector                                  | Directional control effectiveness gradient $\nabla h(\mathbf{x}) \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\mathbf{A}_{\text{cbf}}, \mathbf{b}_{\text{cbf}}$**    | **Barrier Constraint Rows**               | Matrix, Vector                          | Stacked linear constraints $\mathbf{A}_{\text{cbf}}(\mathbf{x})\mathbf{u} \le \mathbf{b}_{\text{cbf}}(\mathbf{x})$ of the CBF-QP; one row is $\mathbf{a}_{\text{cbf}}(\mathbf{x})^\top\mathbf{u} \le b_{\text{cbf}}(\mathbf{x})$.                                                                              |
| **$r$**                                                   | **Barrier Relative Degree**               | Integer                                 | Number of differentiations required before control input $\mathbf{u}$ appears ($L_{\mathbf{g}} L_{\mathbf{f}}^{r-1} h \neq 0$).                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **$h_{\text{kinetic}}(\mathbf{x})$**                      | **Kinetic Inset Barrier Function**        | Scalar                                  | Relative-degree-1 barrier: $h_{\text{kinetic}}(\mathbf{x}) = h(\mathbf{x}) - v^2 / (2 a_{\text{brake}})$ incorporating stopping distance.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\kappa(\cdot)$**                                       | **Class-$\mathcal{K}$ Rate Function**     | Scalar function                         | Extended class-$\mathcal{K}$ function in the barrier condition $\dot{h} \ge -\kappa(h)$; the book uses the linear choice $\kappa(h) = \gamma_{\text{cbf}} h$.                                                                                                                                                  |
| **$\gamma_{\text{cbf}}$**                                 | **Linear Barrier Decay Rate**             | $\text{s}^{-1}$                         | Coefficient of the linear class-$\mathcal{K}$ choice, $\dot{h} + \gamma_{\text{cbf}} h \ge 0$; bare $\gamma$ is the reinforcement-learning discount factor.                                                                                                                                                    |
| **$\mathbf{u}_{\text{nom}} \in \mathcal{U}$**             | **Nominal Control Command**               | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ / $\text{rad}$  | Unverified control candidate proposed across the causal boundary by learned policy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **$\mathbf{u}^* \in \mathcal{U}$**                        | **Certified Control Action**              | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ / $\text{rad}$  | Privileged, safety-filtered control command resolved by the real-time active-set CBF-QP.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **$\alpha(\hat{t})$**                                     | **Bumpless Transfer Blend**               | $[0, 1]$                                | $C^2$ quintic polynomial $6\hat{t}^5 - 15\hat{t}^4 + 10\hat{t}^3$ of normalized time $\hat{t} \in [0, 1]$, ramping between prior and candidate controllers.                                                                                                                                                    |
| **$\tau_{\text{blend}}$**                                 | **Blending Transition Window**            | $\text{s}$                              | Duration of bumpless transfer; bounded by $\tau_{\text{blend}, \min} = 1.875 \lVert \Delta \mathbf{u} \rVert / j_{\max}$.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **$\mathbf{j}(t) = \dot{\mathbf{u}}(t)$**                 | **Control Setpoint Jerk**                 | $\text{m/s}^3, \text{N}\cdot\text{m/s}$ | Time derivative of commanded plant acceleration or actuator torque during mode transitions; its bound is $j_{\max}$.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **$K_p, K_d, K_i$**                                       | **PID / Feedback Gains**                  | Mixed                                   | Proportional, derivative, and integral gains for joint-level or operational-space error stabilization.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **$\mathbf{K}_{\text{lqr}}, \mathbf{Q}_x, \mathbf{R}_u$** | **LQR Gain and Weights**                  | Matrix                                  | State-feedback gain $\mathbf{u}^* = -\mathbf{K}_{\text{lqr}}\mathbf{x}$ and the state and control weights of the quadratic cost; the subscripts keep them distinct from intrinsics, process noise, and rotation.                                                                                               |
| **$\mathbf{D}_{\text{virt}}, \mathbf{K}_{\text{virt}}$**  | **Virtual Damping and Stiffness**         | Matrix                                  | Target impedance/admittance matrices in compliant interaction: $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{safe}} = -\mathbf{D}_{\text{virt}} \dot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q})$.                                                                                                                                        |

:::
